content: Redis keyspace notifications for expired keys are at-most-once/fire-and-forget: subscriber downtime, reconnects, or Redis restarts silently drop events since Pub/Sub state isn't persisted; slow consumers can also lose events on buffer overflow. The 'expired' event fires when Redis actually deletes the key (lazy/active expiry cycle), not exactly at TTL=0, adding delay. For correctness-critical expiry (billing, order/hold timeouts) do not rely on keyspace notification alone - pair it with a periodic DB-side reconciliation sweep (cron) as the source of truth, matching this project's existing hold-expiry design (Redis TTL + cron sweep).
